controllingPriorDecision.whatItEstablished: Retrieved both forms from the Maine Judicial Branch portal at HTTP 200, confirmed both byte-identical to the held copies, read the printed footer revisions, decoded the CR-307 encryption posture from its /P value, and raised the title extraction bug — including the observation that the recorded nextAction's proposed replacement title was itself the other footer line.
controllingPriorDecision.whatThisJobAdds: The title correction itself, taken from each form-face heading by independent re-measurement, together with the statutory citation printed directly beneath each heading, which is the structural marker that distinguishes the heading from every footer line.

method.description: Deterministic in-repository title correction. Each retained binary was opened and its text extracted with layout preserved, and the heading was identified positionally — the block set above the statutory citation and below the caption — rather than by string search, so that neither footer line could be mistaken for it. The result was compared against the adopted edition row, the source-acquisition queue row and the acquisition intelligence.
method.tooling: poppler (pdfinfo, pdftotext -layout) for face text, headings, footers and encryption posture; pdf-lib for AcroForm and page-geometry reads
method.assignmentConstraintObserved: The stop condition requires correcting titles only from each form-face heading and expressly forbids substituting a footer line or changing packet identity without exact evidence. Both titles are taken from the heading block above the statutory citation. Neither footer line is used. No packet identity, role, requirement or binding is changed.

finding.headline: Both Maine titles are wrong in the adopted edition, and they are wrong in two different ways. CR-289's recorded title is not a title at all — it is the form's ADA accessibility notice. CR-307's recorded title happens to be right. The trap is that the obvious correction for CR-289, already written into the acquisition intelligence as a nextAction, is the form's second footer line, which is a third wrong value.
finding.threeCandidateStringsPerForm: Each Maine form offers three plausible title strings: the heading above the statutory citation, footer line 1 (form number and revision), and footer line 2 (a longer descriptive string that inserts the word 'Criminal'). Only the heading is the title.
finding.acquisitionRequiredRationale: Nothing needs to be obtained. Both binaries are retained, both were confirmed against the issuer by the completed dependency, and both headings are legible on the face.

encryptionPosture.publisherAppliedEvidence: The dependency job retrieved the binary fresh from the Maine Judicial Branch portal and found it byte-identical to the retained copy, so the encryption is the publisher's own and not a corpus artefact. This job reproduced the same digest.
encryptionPosture.consequence: Filling the AcroForm fields and printing are both within the permitted set. This does not by itself decide whether the intended generation path is permitted; that remains a question for counsel and is not answered here.

theExtractionBug.shape: Both Maine forms carry a two-line footer. Line 1 is the form number, revision and page count. Line 2 is a longer descriptive string beginning 'Motion to Seal Criminal Conviction for …'. The form's actual heading sits above the statutory citation near the top of the page and contains no word 'Criminal'.
howItProducedThreeDifferentWrongAnswers: CR-289's edition and queue rows took the ADA accessibility notice — a different page-bottom block again, and not even a complete sentence.
The acquisition intelligence took footer line 2 for both forms, which reads as a plausible title and is the reason the recorded nextAction proposes it.
CR-307's edition and queue rows happen to carry the heading, which is correct.
theExtractionBug.correctRule: Take the title from the form-face heading above the statutory citation. Do not take it from either footer line, and do not take it from any page-bottom notice block.
theExtractionBug.structuralMarkerThatMakesThisDeterminist: On both forms the heading is immediately followed by the statutory citation on its own line — '15 M.R.S.A. § 2262-A' for CR-289 and '§ 2262-B' for CR-307. That citation is the anchor: the heading is the block directly above it. This is a positional rule, not a string match, and it survives the fact that three candidate strings all begin with 'Motion to Seal'.
theExtractionBug.wordCriminalIsTheTell: Every wrong candidate that looks like a title contains the word 'Criminal'. Neither heading does. A single-token check will catch this defect anywhere else in the Maine family.

downstreamFieldsThatInheritTheTitle.canonicalRelativePath: Both edition rows embed a slugified title in their canonical relative path, so correcting CR-289's title requires regenerating its path.
downstreamFieldsThatInheritTheTitle.workflowKey: The workflow keys ME:CR-289:MOTION:EN and ME:CR-307:MOTION:EN are keyed on the document id and role rather than the title, so they do not inherit the defect.
downstreamFieldsThatInheritTheTitle.note: The dependency job's recommendation to regenerate the canonical path and workflow key from the corrected title is adopted here only as to the path, because the measured workflow keys do not carry the title.

sourceMaterializationEligibility.laterMaterializationPermittedDetail: Both assets are adopted with canonical paths, pinned digests and byte counts, so receipts are mechanical once the CR-289 title correction lands and its path is regenerated.
sourceMaterializationEligibility.notPermittedYetDetail: Materializing CR-289 against a canonical path slugified from an ADA notice would carry the defect into the runtime contract. Both rows also remain source_gated with release gates open.
sourceMaterializationEligibility.encryptionCaveat: CR-307 is publisher-encrypted with AES-256. Any materialization and rendering path must confirm it can read and fill an encrypted source before relying on it, and the /P value denies modifyContents and assembleDocument.

implementationFamilyEffect.effectOfThisJob: This job is recorded in the live plan as the sole remaining open dependency of rcap-me-acroform-fill. Resolving both titles from the form face removes the reason that job cannot be scheduled, and it forecloses a correction that would have been applied in the wrong direction had the recorded nextAction been followed literally.
implementationFamilyEffect.familyReadinessStatement: The Maine official-PDF family remains fail-closed and this job does not move it. Both assets stay source_gated, the CR-289 title correction has not been applied to the edition, its canonical path still embeds the ADA-notice slug, generation_allowed is unchanged, runtime is disabled and no field map is built. The sibling composed-route job is cancelled and is unaffected.
implementationFamilyEffect.rendererObservation: Both are single-page unrotated Letter AcroForms — 14 fields on CR-289 and 15 on CR-307 — which is the acroform_fill shape. CR-307's publisher encryption is the one complication. An observation about the artifacts; no lane is assigned here.

terminalDispositionDetail.why: The narrowest disposition the evidence supports. It is not unresolved_identity: both documents, issuers, roles, scopes, revisions and titles are established from the artifacts. It is not acquisition_required: both binaries are held and were confirmed against the issuer by the completed dependency. It is not a two-title correction, because CR-307's recorded title is already right and saying otherwise would introduce the very error this job exists to prevent.

expectedDownstreamEffect: Maine's CR-289 stops carrying a truncated ADA accessibility notice as its official title, and its canonical path is flagged for regeneration. CR-307's already-correct title is confirmed rather than disturbed. A recorded nextAction that would have replaced one footer-derived value with another is identified and stopped before it could be applied, and the positional rule that makes the correction deterministic — the heading is the block above the statutory citation — is recorded so the same defect can be caught elsewhere in the Maine family by a single-token check for the word 'Criminal'. The sole remaining open dependency of the Maine acroform-fill job is answered. No component is rebound, no packet identity is changed, no receipt is created, no binary enters version control, no renderer is assigned, no memo is edited, no edition is published, no packet becomes generatable, no runtime is enabled and no track changes promotion state.
